Slide.Title: keep (verb)
Slide.SlideText: keep (verb) Definition: Definition: to possess; to have for oneself Synonyms: Synonyms: hold, have, own, retain Examples: Examples: She decided not to keep the dress she had bought. Slide.Title: kick (verb)
Slide.SlideText: kick (verb) Definition: Definition: to hit with the foot Synonyms: Synonyms: boot, punt Examples: Examples: The children kicked the dry leaves into the air. I accidentally kicked a large rock and broke my toe. The soccer player kicked the ball. The soccer player kicked the ball.

Slide.Title: kidnap (verb)
Slide.SlideText: kidnap (verb) Definition: Definition: to seize (a person) and take away by force Synonyms: Synonyms: abduct, snatch, capture Examples: Examples: Extremists kidnapped the president’s wife. Slide.Title: kind (noun)

Slide.Title: kind (adjective)
Slide.SlideText: kind (adjective) Definition: Definition: gentle, caring, helpful Synonyms: Synonyms: benevolent, compassionate, generous, good Examples: Examples: She taught her children to be kind to animals. Slide.Title: kiss (verb)

Slide.Title: knowledge (noun)
Slide.SlideText: knowledge (noun) Definition: Definition: that which is known; learning or understanding Synonyms: Synonyms: learning, wisdom, comprehension, education Examples: Examples: I have no knowledge about their plans.
